summary: Terahertz spectroscopy is used to map wafer-scale homogeneity of NbTiN thin films on 4-inch and 6-inch Si wafers grown by plasma-enhanced magnetron sputtering, measuring sheet resistance $R_s$ at room temperature via THz-FDS and superconducting properties at cryogenic temperatures via THz-TDS. Room-temperature $R_s$ variations (1.77–7.78% standard deviation) correlate with film thickness and deposition device, while the zero-temperature sheet kinetic inductance $L_{k0}$ follows $R_s$ variations, but critical temperature $T_c$ (13.68–13.81 K) and energy gap $2\Delta_0$ remain uniform across the wafer.
motivation: Homogeneous superconducting thin films are essential for reproducible large-scale device fabrication in quantum computing and sensing platforms, yet standard characterization requires lithography and electrical contacts.
method: NbTiN films of thicknesses 5–60 nm on Si substrates were characterized by THz-FDS (9–10.5 cm$^{-1}$, room temperature) for $R_s$ mapping and THz-TDS (300 GHz–3 THz, down to 1.5 K) on diced samples for optical conductivity and superconducting parameters via Mattis-Bardeen theory fits.
result: For films thicker than 30 nm, $R_s$ uniformity plateaus with standard deviation $\sim$0.6–0.7%, while sub-30 nm films show degraded homogeneity (up to 7.78%); $L_{k0}$ deviations match $R_s$ deviations ($\delta L_{k0} \propto \delta R_s$), enabling prediction of device performance from room-temperature measurements, but $T_c$ and $2\Delta_0$ show minimal spatial variation ($<$0.1 K and meV scales).
